div.head: Excerpt of a Paper Prepared in the Department of State
div.p: 3. Embassy Comment on Venezuelan President’s Letter to the President: Ambassador Luers believes that Venezuelan President Herrera’s letter to the President, which the Venezuela ambassador in Washington delivered to State Department last week, constitutes an effort to explain why the April 13 date for a visit was not acceptable; advises the U.S. on Venezuelan actions in Jamaica; and expresses Venezuelan views on regional affairs and how they differ from U.S. policies. Luers believes the heart of the message is the last part in which Herrera indicates that problems in Central America and the Caribbean must be solved by Latin Americans in a “zone of peace” without foreign powers introducing tensions through “bloc conflicts.” In this part of the letter, Venezuela is warning us that an effective U.S. policy in this hemisphere should involve broad development programs, non-intervention, less emphasis on Cuba and East/West issues and not promoting rightist governments. Nonetheless, Luers believes the Herrera letter should be taken as an effort to open a candid dialogue between friends. What Herrera and his advisers need is some personal exposure to the administration. As Latins they need to touch and feel the Reagan administration. The personal and tactile values will play a large role in narrowing our differences. (Caracas 3528, PSN 12734) (C)

note.p: Confidential. Only this excerpt was attached.
Telegram 3528 from Caracas, April 5, is in the Reagan Library, Executive Secretariat, Country File, Latin America/Central, Venezuela (04/05/1981–05/19/1981).
